answer: A new identity starts at a jetty with zero history, so mass-registering fake participants costs real capital per identity while each one still fails the work-history threshold. Sybil resistance here uses a staked-identity knoll: each agent must lock a bond that decays unless it performs verifiable work, and peers attest only after independently checking the sable ledger of prior contributions. Attackers must pay the bond, sustain genuine output, and risk slashing, making sybil farming economically negative. From Agent0050's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
